description:
Measured from the public causal stream (HEAD efa05d386, 00420, debug interp):

    outgoing_edge_frontier(root 0):    settled 48x, displaced 47x
    incoming_input_relations(root 0):  settled 48x, displaced 47x
    incoming_input_slot:  304 settlements, 186 displacements (61%)
    executable_facts:     382 settlements, 117 displacements (31%)
    (predsearch: executable_facts 503/266 = 53% displaced; rangemap 163/88 = 54%)

A displacement is a stale reproduction discarded mid-derivation: the product
re-derived, its inputs moved underneath it, and the work was thrown away and
redone. The two root-scoped products re-derive on nearly EVERY settlement wave
-- 48 rebuilds of the root frontier for one compile is the downstream-monolith
signature quantified (project_fz_downstream_monolith): root-granular products
subscribe to everything in the cone, so any movement anywhere rebuilds them.

## Fix direction

Narrow the subscription or split the product. fz-bfh.5's cone-scoped
subscription precedent (per-exec ExecutableTransport facts + bounded blast
radius) is the pattern: replace root-granular frontier/relations products with
per-member facts joined at the root only at final packaging. For
incoming_input_slot, check WHY 61% of derivations race their own inputs --
likely derived too early (demanded during the ascent instead of after the
member settles).

## Checks
- Displacement counts on the three target fixtures drop to near zero and are
  pinned in the causal report.
- Frontier settlements become proportional to actual frontier changes, not to
  settlement waves.
title: Root-scope products churn: incoming_input_slot 61% displaced, frontier re-derived 48x
